stem: Which additional recommendation should the nurse include when teaching new parents how to reduce the risk of sleep-related infant death?

options.A: Share an adult bed with the infant overnight for closer monitoring.
options.B: Place pillows and loose blankets in the sleep space to keep the infant warm.
options.C: Avoid smoke and nicotine exposure, prevent overheating, and offer a pacifier at naps and bedtime; if breastfeeding, wait until breastfeeding is established before introducing the pacifier.
options.D: Allow secondhand smoke exposure because it is not associated with SIDS risk.

rationale: Current CDC safe-sleep guidance explicitly supports the AAP 2022 recommendations: avoid smoke and nicotine exposure, avoid overheating, and offer a pacifier at naps and bedtime. For a breastfed infant, pacifier introduction should wait until breastfeeding is established. Adult bed-sharing and soft bedding are not recommended safe-sleep practices. C is correct.
educational_objective: Teach evidence-based safe-sleep measures beyond supine positioning and a firm sleep surface.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), supporting American Academy of Pediatrics recommendations
source_document_title: Providing Care for Babies to Sleep Safely
source_locator: Creating a safe sleep area for babies; Additional recommendations to reduce the risk of SIDS
source_claim_supported: Avoid smoke/nicotine exposure and overheating; offer a pacifier at nap time and bedtime, delaying introduction until breastfeeding is established for breastfed infants; avoid bed-sharing and soft bedding.

source_original.stem: A nurse is providing SIDS (Sudden Infant Death Syndrome) risk reduction education to new parents. In addition to safe sleep positioning, the nurse should include which additional recommendation?

options.A: Share an adult bed with the infant overnight so the parent can continuously monitor breathing
options.B: Use pillows and thick blankets in the sleep space to prevent the infant from becoming cold
options.C: Avoid smoke and overheating and consider a pacifier for sleep once breastfeeding is established
options.D: Permit secondhand smoke exposure because tobacco smoke is not associated with sleep-related death

source_original.rationale: In addition to safe sleep positioning (back to sleep, firm surface), comprehensive SIDS risk reduction education includes avoiding infant exposure to smoke, offering a pacifier at sleep time (once breastfeeding is well-established, generally around 3-4 weeks), and avoiding overheating/overbundling the infant — all evidence-based recommendations from the AAP, while bed-sharing is not recommended.
source_original.source_detail: AAP safe-sleep recommendations: smoke avoidance, pacifier at sleep, avoid overheating and bed-sharing; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Updated currentness with CDC's 2024 page explicitly supporting the AAP 2022 recommendations, removed the unsupported fixed '3-4 weeks' timing because breastfeeding establishment varies, and retained only current safe-sleep recommendations.
